title_candidates: Hugging Face says users should rotate access tokens
summary: After an AI-driven intrusion reached internal datasets and service credentials, Hugging Face recommends rotating access tokens and reviewing account activity.

primary_source.title: Security incident disclosure - July 2026
primary_source.author: Hugging Face
key_facts: A malicious dataset exploited code-execution paths and allowed an autonomous attack framework to move into internal clusters.
Hugging Face found no evidence of tampering with public models, datasets, Spaces, packages, or container images.
The company is still assessing possible partner or customer impact.
Hugging Face recommends rotating access tokens and reviewing recent activity.

supporting_sources.title: User access tokens
key_facts: Tokens can be refreshed or deleted, and Hugging Face recommends separate fine-grained tokens for production apps.

supporting_sources.title: Hugging Face Hub security
key_facts: The Hub supports two-factor authentication and other account security controls.

prerequisites: Access to services using its tokens

steps.instruction: Open Access Tokens and delete credentials you cannot identify.
Refresh required tokens and narrow each one to the app's actual permissions.
Replace old secrets, test each service, enable 2FA, and review repository changes.

risk_flags: The investigation remains open, so the article avoids claiming that all customer data was unaffected.
